Philippines நாட்டின் AFASA விதிமுறைகளுக்கு இணங்கவும், மோசடிகளைத் தடுக்கவும் அடையாள சரிபார்ப்பு, AML ஸ்கிரீனிங் மற்றும் நிகழ்நேர பரிவர்த்தனை கண்காணிப்பு போன்ற வசதிகள் இந்த கூட்டாண்மை மூலம் ஒருங்கிணைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளன.

title: Lovey Announces £250M Senior Secured Credit Facility With Pollen Street Capital
summary:
Lovey, the UK’s fastest-growing fintech and financial services provider, specialising in SME lending and brokerage, has today announced a senior secured credit facility of up to £250 million with Pollen Street Capital (“Pollen Street”), an alternative asset manager. The facility is made up of £50 million committed capital and a £200 million accordion, making it the largest funding facility in Lovey's history and marking a key milestone in the company's growth.
 
The facility demonstrates continued institutional investor confidence in Lovey's lending model, technology and long-term strategy and reinforces Lovey's position as a leading finance provider focusing on SME funding. The facility will significantly increase Lovey’s lending capacity, supporting the business as it scales its own-book lending while continuing to grow its established brokerage proposition.
 
Founded by Jack Smith in 2016, Lovey has grown from a one-person start-up into a 120-strong business, funding more than £600 million in loans to over 11,000 UK SMEs. Built around a mission to make lending simple, fast and beautiful, Lovey has expanded rapidly while staying focused on making finance easier and more accessible for small businesses. The new facility will support that mission by giving Lovey the capital to help more UK SMEs access funding quickly and flexibly.
 
Lovey began lending directly from its own balance sheet in 2022, building on its experience as a broker to develop a deeper understanding of the funding needs of UK SMEs. Today, the business combines direct lending with its established brokerage proposition, giving customers access to both Lovey’s own lending and a wider panel of funding partners. This approach allows Lovey to match businesses with the funding solution that best suits their needs, while the new facility provides greater capacity to grow its direct lending operation.
 
Jack Smith, Founder and CEO at Lovey, comments:
 
“This new facility is an important milestone for us and will enable us to put more capital behind UK small businesses, scale our own-book lending and give more SMEs access to finance when they need it. Pollen Street shares our belief that finances for small businesses should be simpler, faster and more flexible, and we’re really pleased to have them backing Lovey for this next stage of growth.”
 
Kai Hunter, Chief Operating Officer at Lovey, comments:
 
“The funding announced today is the result of close and collaborative work with Pollen Street and I am grateful to their team, and to our own, for the diligence they brought to it. This funding deepens our lending capacity and allows us to offer larger loans, so that we can back more of the UK’s small and medium-sized businesses, from those that have found finance hardest to secure to the well-established, with greater speed and certainty.”
 
Ethan Saggu, Investment Director, Pollen Street, adds:
 
“Lovey has spent almost a decade seeing the UK SME lending market from a broker’s perspective, giving the team an expert view of where demand for credit is going unmet. We have financed a number of specialist SME lenders and recognise what it takes to grow from brokerage into balance-sheet lending. Lovey has done so with a well-defined product and a focused approach, and we look forward to supporting the team as it scales.”
 
Lovey was advised by Ashurst Perkins Coie and Pollen Street was advised by Simmons & Simmons.
 
The facility builds on Lovey's existing funding arrangements announced last year, including a £35 million revolving credit facility from Paragon Bank and a £10 million junior medium-term note programme from LGB Capital Markets. The new facility also adds to Lovey's growing institutional funding base as it enters its next phase of expansion.

title: House Oversight Chair Comer Probes Delaware Plan for AI-Run Companies

title: Avail launches ShieldTX privacy tool targeting copy-trading bots on Hyperliquid
summary: Avail launched ShieldTX, a Hyperliquid privacy tool that creates a separate wallet for each perpetual futures position.
content: Avail has launched ShieldTX, a new privacy tool designed specifically to target copy-trading bots on the Hyperliquid platform. The tool works by generating a separate, distinct wallet for every individual perpetual futures position created by users. This innovation aims to enhance user privacy and prevent automated bots from tracking and copying trading strategies on the network.
content_ta: Hyperliquid платфорமில் காப்பி-ட்ரேடிங்போட்களை குறிவைத்து Avail நிறுவனம் ShieldTX என்ற புதிய பிரைவசி டூலை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. பயனர்கள் உருவாக்கும் ஒவ்வொரு பெர்ச்சுவல் ஃபியூச்சர்ஸ் பொசிஷனுக்கும் தனித்தனி வாலட்டை உருவாக்குவதன் மூலம் இந்த டூல் செயல்படுகிறது. இந்த புதிய தொழில்நுட்பம் பயனர்களின் தனியுரிமையை பாதுகாக்கவும், பாட்கள் வர்த்தக வியூகங்களை பின்தொடர்வதை தடுக்கவும் உதவுகிறது.

title: Crypto braces for potential shift in congressional oversight after midterms
summary: Post-Clarity Act, the crypto sector could find itself navigating a very different political landscape under a new Congress.
content: The crypto sector is preparing for a potential shift in congressional oversight following the midterm elections. Following developments around the Clarity Act, industry participants could find themselves navigating a very different political landscape under a newly composed United States Congress, which may impact future regulatory approaches and legislative priorities for digital assets.
content_ta: இடைத்தேர்தல்களுக்குப் பிறகு காங்கிரஸ் மேற்பார்வையில் ஏற்படக்கூடிய சாத்தியமான மாற்றத்திற்கு கிரிப்டோ துறை தயாராகி வருகிறது. Clarity Act தொடர்பான முன்னேற்றங்களைத் தொடர்ந்து, புதிதாகத் தேர்ந்தெடுக்கப்பட்ட United States காங்கிரஸ் அமைப்பின் கீழ், டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துக்களுக்கான எதிர்கால ஒழுங்குமுறை அணுகுமுறைகளையும் சட்டப்பூர்வ முன்னுரிமைகளையும் பாதிக்கக்கூடிய மிகவும் வித்தியாசமான அரசியல் சூழலை இத்துறை எதிர்கொள்ள நேரிடும்.

title: Ripple expects $900 million annualized product revenue run rate as institutional business expands
summary: Ripple expects a $900M annualized product revenue run rate by end of 2026, as RLUSD reaches $2.5B and payments near $150B in lifetime volume.
content: Ripple anticipates reaching a $900 million annualized product revenue run rate as its institutional business continues to expand. The company projects significant growth supported by strong adoption of RLUSD and expanding lifetime payment volumes.
content_ta: Ripple தனது institutional வணிகம் விரிவடைவதால், $900 million வருடாந்திர product revenue run rate-ஐ எட்டும் என்று எதிர்பார்க்கிறது. RLUSD-ன் வலுவான பயன்பாடு மற்றும் payment volume அதிகரிப்பு ஆகியவற்றின் மூலம் இந்த வளர்ச்சி கிடைக்கும் என நிறுவனம் கருதுகிறது.

title: Bitcoin option buyers face a Fed-week premium that can fade after the decision
summary:
Laevitas’s Oct. 26 snapshot showed a 9.2-point implied-versus-realized premium, putting buyers’ exposure after policy decisions in focus.
Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: Bitcoin option buyers are currently facing a high implied-versus-realized premium ahead of the upcoming Federal Reserve policy decision. Data from Laevitas indicates that this premium highlights significant market exposure for traders holding positions through the rate announcement. Once the central bank makes its decision, this risk premium is expected to fade.
content_ta: வரவிருக்கும் Fed கொள்கை முடிவைத் தொடர்ந்து பிட்காய்ட் ஆப்ஷன் வாங்குபவர்கள் அதிக பிரீமியத்தை எதிர்கொண்டு வருகின்றனர். Laevitas தரவுகளின்படி, இந்த பிரீமியம் வர்த்தகர்களின் சந்தை வெளிப்பாட்டை எடுத்துக்காட்டுகிறது. மத்திய வங்கி தனது முடிவை அறிவித்தவுடன், இந்த பிரீமியம் குறைய வாய்ப்புள்ளது.

title: Kraken to cancel orders across 176 crypto markets in sweeping trading overhaul
summary:
Existing orders will not transfer to synthetic replacements, where limit orders will carry taker fees.
Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: Cryptocurrency exchange Kraken is overhauling its trading system by canceling orders across numerous markets. Existing orders will not be transferred to new synthetic replacements, and limit orders will now be subject to taker fees. This update marks a significant shift in how trading operations and order books are managed on the platform.
content_ta: கிரிப்டோகரன்சி எக்ஸ்சேஞ்ச் ஆன Kraken தனது வர்த்தக அமைப்பில் பெரிய மாற்றங்களைச் செய்து வருகிறது, இதன் ஒரு பகுதியாக பல சந்தைகளில் உள்ள ஆர்டர்கள் ரத்து செய்யப்படுகின்றன. தற்போதுள்ள ஆர்டர்கள் புதிய செயற்கை மாற்றீடுகளுக்கு மாற்றப்படாது, மேலும் லிமிட் ஆர்டர்களுக்கு டேக்கர் கட்டணம் வசூலிக்கப்படும். இந்த அறிவிப்பு பிளாட்ஃபார்மில் வர்த்தக நடவடிக்கைகளில் ஒரு முக்கிய மாற்றத்தைக் குறிக்கிறது.

title: Coinbase Sets October 30 Deadline for Restricted Stablecoins in EEA
summary: Coinbase has warned retail users in the European Economic Area to withdraw affected non-MiCA-compliant stablecoins by October 30, 2026.
content: Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase has issued a warning to its retail users within the European Economic Area. The company has set an October 30 deadline for customers to withdraw affected stablecoins that do not comply with the region's new regulatory framework, ahead of future policy changes.
content_ta: கிரிப்டோகரன்சி எக்ஸ்சேஞ்ச் ஆன Coinbase, ஐரோப்பிய பொருளாதாரப் பகுதிக்குள் (EEA) உள்ள சில்லறை பயனர்களுக்கு எச்சரிக்கை விடுத்துள்ளது. புதிய ஒழுங்குமுறை விதிகளுக்கு இணங்காத ஸ்டேபிள்காயின்களை வாடிக்கையாளர்கள் அக்டோபர் 30 ஆம் தேதிக்குள் திரும்பப் பெறுமாறு கெடு விதிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: Confidential ZEC trading goes live on Shield
summary: Traders can now buy, sell, and provide liquidity for ZEC while keeping their identity, portfolio, and trading strategies confidential. Shield has launched the first confidential onchain trading pair for ZEC, allowing users to manage their Zcash alongside other assets in its non-custodial wallet. The new pair gives ZEC holders access to a confidential, non-custodial AMM where they can buy, sell, and provide liquidity without publishing their wallet activity to the market. The launch expands Shield’s supported markets through its concentrated-liquidity AMM on Aleo. With this launch, Shield adds ZEC support to its non-custodial wallet, allowing users to manage the asset alongside their other supported holdings. How Zcash protects transaction data Zcash launched in October 2016 with support for transparent and shielded transactions. Transparent addresses work much like Bitcoin addresses. Their balances and transaction histories are publicly visible. Shielded transactions encrypt the sender, recipient, and amount, while allowing the network to verify that each transaction follows its rules. Zcash was the first widespread application of zkSNARKs, demonstrating that a decentralized network could verify transactions without publishing the underlying financial information. ZEC on Shield ZEC trades for USDCx in a concentrated-liquidity pool. Traders can move between ZEC and a dollar-denominated asset, and liquidity providers can supply capital within their chosen price ranges. Shield Swap runs on Aleo, combining publicly verifiable market state with encrypted wallet records. Zero-knowledge proofs allow the network to verify transactions without exposing confidential wallet data. Traders can inspect prices and available liquidity before confirming a swap. Liquidity providers can evaluate the pool before deciding where to allocate capital. Pool reserves, prices, trade sizes, and fees remain publicly verifiable. Shield Swap protects your identity, portfolio, and trading strategies. Wallet balances, portfolio composition, and links between trades remain confidential. Protecting ZEC portfolios Trading on a transparent chain creates a permanent history associated with wallet addresses. Once an address is associated with a trader, its balances and transaction history become available to anyone following the market. Fresh addresses can make analysis harder, but trade sizes, timing, and repeated behavior can still provide clues that connect activity. Over time, those connections can reveal how a trader builds a position, rebalances a portfolio, or moves capital between assets. Shield Swap addresses this exposure. Public market data does not provide a direct view into each participant’s wallet and broader portfolio. For ZEC holders, this means access to onchain trading without making their wallet history part of the market information available to competitors. Providing liquidity for ZEC/USDCx The ZEC/USDCx pool lets traders move between ZEC and a dollar-denominated asset. Liquidity providers choose the price ranges in which they want their capital to be available for trading and earn fees when their liquidity is used. This gives providers control over how they allocate capital. A narrower range concentrates capital around selected prices. A wider range makes liquidity available across more prices. Providers can adjust their positions as market conditions and their objectives change. ZEC in your Shield wallet Shield’s non-custodial wallet now supports ZEC. Users can manage ZEC alongside other supported assets and connect their wallet to Shield to trade or provide liquidity. A 1-click banner prompt moves assets into the wallet’s shielded balance so they are ready to trade. Wallet balances are held in encrypted records, and users retain control of their keys and funds. Shield currently covers Aleo network fees for swaps. The liquidity-provider fee is included in the quote before the user approves the trade. ZEC/USDCx trading is available on Shield. Early access is open to eligible organizations and individual market participants. Visit swap.shield.fi to access the market or shield.fi/docs for documentation. Shield is a technology provider. It is not a broker, dealer, or registered intermediary, and does not provide investment, legal, tax, or other advice of any kind. Participants act on their own account and remain responsible for their trading decisions and compliance with applicable law.
content: Shield has launched confidential ZEC trading and liquidity provision through a new ZEC/USDCx pool on the Aleo network. The non-custodial platform uses zero-knowledge proofs to let users trade and manage Zcash while keeping their identities, portfolio balances, and trading strategies private.
content_ta: Aleo நெட்வொர்க்கில் புதிய ZEC/USDCx பூல் மூலம் ரகசியமான ZEC வர்த்தகம் மற்றும் பணப்புழக்க சேவையை Shield அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. ஜீரோ-நெட்வொர்க் ப்ரூஃப்ஸ் தொழில்நுட்பத்தைப் பயன்படுத்தி, பயனர்கள் தங்கள் அடையாளங்கள், போர்ட்ஃபோலியோ இருப்பு மற்றும் வர்த்தக உத்திகளை ரகசியமாகப் பாதுகாத்துக்கொண்டு Zcash-ஐ வர்த்தகம் செய்து நிர்வகிக்க இந்த நான்-கஸ்டோடியல் தளம் அனுமதிக்கிறது.

title: C2FO and Ripple Bring Instant-Pay Settlement Plans to XRP Ledger
summary: C2FO and Ripple say their Instant Pay initiative will use the XRP Ledger and RLUSD to settle financing associated with approved supplier invoices.
content: C2FO and Ripple have announced a partnership to introduce Instant Pay settlement plans utilizing the XRP Ledger. The initiative is designed to use the XRP Ledger and RLUSD to handle the settlement of financing related to approved supplier invoices, aiming to streamline transactions and improve financial efficiency for businesses.
content_ta: C2FO மற்றும் Ripple நிறுவனங்கள் இணைந்து XRP Ledger-ஐப் பயன்படுத்தி Instant Pay தீர்வு திட்டங்களை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளன. ஒப்புதல் அளிக்கப்பட்ட சப்ளையர் இன்வாய்ஸ்களுடன் தொடர்புடைய நிதியுதவியை தீர்க்க XRP Ledger மற்றும் RLUSD-ஐப் பயன்படுத்துவதே இந்தத் திட்டத்தின் நோக்கமாகும்.

title: XRP, HYPE, and ENA Levels to Watch Before the Fed Meets Today: Analyst
summary: XRP's inverse head-and-shoulders pattern could point higher, but a daily close above $1.55 may be needed before $2.10 comes into view.
content: As analysts watch key levels for XRP, HYPE, and ENA ahead of today's Federal Reserve meeting, technical patterns emerge for major tokens. Specifically, XRP displays an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern that could signal upward momentum. However, traders note that a solid daily close above the $1.55 resistance level may be necessary before aiming for the $2.10 target.
content_ta: இன்றைய Federal Reserve கூட்டத்திற்கு முன்னதாக XRP, HYPE மற்றும் ENA ஆகியவற்றின் முக்கிய நிலைகளை ஆய்வாளர்கள் கவனித்து வருகின்றனர். குறிப்பாக்க், XRP-ல் உள்ள இன்வெர்ஸ் ஹெட் அண்ட் ஷோல்டர்ஸ் பேட்டர்ன் மேல்நோக்கிய இயக்கத்தைக் குறிக்கலாம். இருப்பினும், $2.10 இலக்கை எட்டுவதற்கு முன்பு $1.55-க்கு மேல் தினசரி முடிவு தேவைப்படலாம் என்று வர்த்தகர்கள் குறிப்பிடுகின்றனர்.

title: 21Shares withdraws $11M in POL over 30 days – Polygon reclaims $0.09
summary: 21Shares withdrew 45.7 million POL, worth $4.08 million, from Coinbase.
content: Investment firm 21Shares withdrew millions in POL tokens from Coinbase over a 30-day period. The substantial transfer involved tens of millions of the cryptocurrency, valued at several million dollars. Following these market movements, the Polygon network token saw a price movement reclaiming a specific key valuation level.
content_ta: இன்வெஸ்ட்மென்ட் நிறுவனமான 21Shares, 30 நாட்களுக்குள் Coinbase தளத்தில் இருந்து லட்சக்கணக்கான POL டோக்கன்களை திரும்பப் பெற்றுள்ளது. இந்த குறிப்பிடத்தக்க பரிமாற்றத்தில் பல மில்லியன் ட மதிப்புள்ள கோடிக்கணக்கான கிரிப்டோகரன்சி உள்ளடங்கியுள்ளது. இந்தச் சந்தை நகர்வுகளுக்குப் பிறகு, Polygon நெட்வொர்க் டோக்கன் அதன் முக்கிய விலைமதிப்பை மீண்டும் எட்டியுள்ளது.

title: Why crypto transfers have both an asset and a network
summary: ETH can appear on Ethereum and on Arbitrum One, yet the two networks keep separate records of its movement. A cryptocurrency name therefore gives only part of a transfer’s description. It identifies the asset, while the network identifies where the transaction takes place. That distinction explains why a wallet or payment service can display bothContinue reading "Why crypto transfers have both an asset and a network"
content: Cryptocurrency transfers require identifying both an asset and a network. For example, ETH can exist on both Ethereum and Arbitrum One, with each network maintaining separate movement records. A cryptocurrency name specifies the asset, while the network indicates where the transaction occurs, explaining how digital wallets and payment services process these distinct layers.
content_ta: கிரிப்டோகரன்சி பரிமாற்றங்களுக்கு ஒரு அசெட் மற்றும் நெட்வொர்க் இரண்டையும் குறிப்பிடுவது அவசியமாகும். உதாரணமாக, ETH ஆனது Ethereum மற்றும் Arbitrum One இரண்டிலும் இயங்க முடியும், மேலும் ஒவ்வொரு நெட்வொர்க்கும் அதன் பரிமாற்ற பதிவுகளை தனித்தனியாக பராமரிக்கிறது. கிரிப்டோகரன்சி பெயர் அசெட்டை அடையாளம் காட்டுகிறது, அதே நேரத்தில் நெட்வொர்க் பரிவர்த்தனை எங்கு நடக்கிறது என்பதைக் குறிக்கிறது.

title: 'DOGE Was Never Meant to Be Ethereum or Solana': Dogecoin Contributor Sets Record Straight
summary: Dogecoin contributor defends its original purpose, saying its  simplicity remains strength.
content: A Dogecoin contributor has clarified the original purpose of the cryptocurrency, stating that it was never designed to compete with platforms like Ethereum or Solana. Responding to ongoing discussions in the digital asset community, the contributor emphasized that Dogecoin's simplicity remains its greatest strength and core identity, rather than complex smart contract capabilities.
content_ta: Dogecoin-ன் உண்மையான நோக்கம் என்ன என்பது குறித்து அதன் பங்களிப்பாளர் ஒருவர் விளக்கம் அளித்துள்ளார். Ethereum அல்லது Solana போன்ற பிளாட்பாரங்களுடன் போட்டியிடும் வகையில் Dogecoin எப்போதுமே உருவாக்கப்படவில்லை என்று அவர் தெரிவித்துள்ளார். கிரிப்டோகரன்சி சமூகத்தில் நிலவி வரும் விவாதங்களுக்கு மத்தியில், Dogecoin-ன் எளிமையே அதன் மிகப்பெரிய பலமாகவும் அதன் அடையாளமாகவும் தொடர்கிறது என்று அவர் குறிப்பிட்டுள்ளார்.

title: Coinbase Launches Ripple USD, Challenging Kraken's Market Hold
summary: Ripple’s new RLUSD stablecoin lands Coinbase, a move which may force a major liquidity reshuffle for U.S. regulated corporate cash.

title: A16z’s crypto predictions aged like milk

content_ta: தனது முந்தைய தொழில்துறை கணிப்புகள் குறித்த மறுபரிசீலனைக்குப் பிறகு, A16z நிறுவனம் தனது முக்கிய கிரிப்டோகரன்சி நிதியை ஒரு ஃபிரண்டியர் ஃபண்டாக மறுபெயரிட்டுள்ளது. சந்தை நிலவரங்கள் மாறியதால் அந்த கணிப்புகள் சரியாக பொருந்தவில்லை என்று ஊடகச் செய்திகள் சுட்டிக்காட்டியுள்ளன. இந்த நடவடிக்கையானது, முக்கிய வென்ச்சர் கேப்பிட்டல் நிறுவனம் தனது டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து முதலீடுகளை நிர்வகிக்கும் விதத்தில் ஒரு மூலோபாய மாற்றத்தைக் கொண்டுவந்துள்ளது.

title: Ant International CEO: AI to Drive ‘Re-Globalisation’ by Democratising Global Access
summary:
Speaking at the United Nations Trade and Development (UNCTAD) World Investment Forum 2026 panel, “Investing in AI for an Inclusive Digital Future”, Ant International CEO Peng Yang called for a new, inclusive “re-globalisation” project that harnesses AI and digital connectivity to give small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) greater access to global markets and opportunities.
“Globalisation 1.0 mostly benefited large enterprises, and a lot of SMEs very rarely got to participate in the global economy,” said Yang. “Achieving inclusion is critical to re-globalisation, and AI will accelerate it by democratising opportunities.”

Ant International CEO Peng Yang speaks at the United Nations Trade and Development (UNCTAD) World Investment Forum 2026
The limitation of Globalisation 1.0 and how AI and other innovations offer a chance to improve
Yang said one of the greatest limitations of Globalisation 1.0 was its concentration of power among large enterprises. Small businesses, which make up over 90% of businesses globally, have often been left behind due to the gap in technologies, talent and other resources. It is difficult for them to participate in the last round of globalisation, which involves handling multiple markets and the complexities of global trade.
According to the WTO’s 2024 World Trade Report, 8% of small firms and 15% of medium-sized firms export directly, compared with 30% of large firms.
The AI divide compounds the challenge: a 2025 survey by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) shows 52% of large firms used AI, compared with just 17.4% of small firms.
However, the rise of AI means we have the chance to level the field and close the gap if we democratise AI technology and its applications to give equal opportunities to SMEs.
When innovation meets inclusion, SMEs can also grow and thrive on the global stage
Yang said that in the past three years, Ant International has been serving over 1 million new small merchants from 54 new markets globally, empowering them to participate in global trade.
“In the last three years, we have seen tremendous growth for SMEs when innovation meets inclusion. When we offer them powerful full-stack AI-native solutions, cross-border transaction volume of SMEs across our own businesses has been growing by about 50% every year, which is 10 times the growth rate of the total volume of global trade,” he said.
“This shows that if we can do things right, drive innovation, provide the AI technologies, and make it more accessible for the small guys, they can take the global stage to grow and thrive,” Yang added.
Ant International processes 25 million transactions daily across its global payment, global account, embedded finance and digitalisation services. 95% of its 150 million-strong global merchant customer base are SMEs. In September 2026, Ant International announced sweeping full-stack AI-native solutions on payment, account, FX, treasury and growth for global businesses, many designed to tackle SMEs’ challenges. 

Ant International CEO Peng Yang (center) at a panel in the United Nations Trade and Development (UNCTAD) World Investment Forum 2026
New full-stack AI-native solutions empowering SMEs to drive truly inclusive re-globalisation
Democratising the Falcon TST FX model for SMEs
Cross-border FX and money management is expensive for SMEs. Ant International has been developing its Falcon TST AI forecast model, which achieved SOTA (state-of-the-art performance) on the MASE metric on a top global benchmark, with a consistent forecast accuracy rate of over 93%, and has been working with the world’s leading banks to keep increasing coverage. Today, it has been democratised as part of the full-stack AI-native solutions for SMEs to use so they can handle global transactions more efficiently with less FX risk.
Proprietary agents WorldFirst Autopilot and Antom Autopilot automate operations for SMEs
Under WorldFirst and Antom – Ant International’s core Global Account and Global Payment services – enterprise-grade financial capabilities are engineered into SME-friendly applications. 
WorldFirst combines cross-border collections, payments, foreign exchange and fund management in one global account. This enables smaller businesses to manage international operations, collect money and make payments with less FX risk and access working capital at lower cost, even without finance and treasury teams. Ant International’s global AI business agent for SMEs — WorldFirst Autopilot — further simplifies the operations by streamlining financial tasks and connecting businesses to partner services through natural language interactions.
WorldFirst helps over 2 million SMEs to manage their cross-border accounts, with more than US$500 billion in cumulative transaction volume across 210+ markets. Its network connects SMEs to 130+ e-commerce platforms and 600+ ecosystem partners, helping them navigate overseas markets and grow globally. 
Antom Autopilot simplifies payment operations for merchants, especially SMEs, with AI support across onboarding, integration, analysis, risk management and reconciliation. By the end of 2026, 95% of merchants are expected to complete onboarding with Antom within 1 hour. Its SmartDispute provides dispute analysis and appeal strategies, helping merchants achieve a 41.8% win rate versus 24.5% without the tool, while its fully automated AutoDispute helps merchants recover an average of 18% of chargeback losses, reducing the additional resources SMEs need to devote to dispute management.
Alipay+ empowers SMEs to access global consumers with AI-powered marketing solutions
For Global Payment, Alipay+, Ant International’s global wallet gateway, connects over 50 digital wallets to more than 150 million merchants globally, over 95% of them SMEs. Beyond seamless cross-border payments, small merchants are targeting global consumers online and in-store with more effective and precise campaigns through Alipay+’s AI-powered marketing solutions.
In the Siam Square commercial area in Bangkok, Thailand, the Alipay+ marketing campaign combining pre-trip social-media push and on-site ad displays helped small merchants grow TPV by 66% YoY, with an increase in the number of orders by 115% YoY; for merchants in Gaya Street in Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia, it drove more than 120% growth in TPV and 140% in orders; for a local skincare brand in Bali, Indonesia, it delivered a growth of 137% in TPV and 140% in orders during the campaign.
New foundations of trust for inclusive AI in public-private sector collaboration
Yang also stressed that businesses, including SMEs, need confidence that AI can be used safely and responsibly, particularly as AI agents take on financial and operational tasks. Effective safeguards require collaboration across the technology and financial industries, alongside regulators and international institutions.
“Trust is everything in payments and financial services, and it becomes even more critical in the AI era. We need to work closely with international organisations and regulators to develop appropriate frameworks, while building safeguards that allow businesses to use AI agents safely. Collaboration across the private sector must also be complemented by international institutions and regulators to establish common standards and trusted infrastructure,” said Yang.
Ant International is advancing this approach through collaboration across the public and private sectors. In Singapore, it works with the Infocomm Media Development Authority on privacy-enhancing technologies and participates in the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s BuildFin.ai initiative on developing and scaling responsible AI solutions for financial services. 
The company is also collaborating with Visa and Mastercard on interoperability for Know Your Agent (KYA), helping strengthen trust in AI agents acting on behalf of consumers and businesses.
It also takes a step forward by introducing the industry-first Antom AgentSafePay, built to protect merchants navigating agentic commerce, to verify multi-dimensional purchase intent in real time, and to offer a fund guarantee against losses from intent misinterpretation, malicious prompt injection or other risks within merchant-deployed agents.
Yang said that, with the cost of AI lowered and accessibility made easier for SMEs, both small merchants and individuals can be equipped with enterprise-grade innovative solutions, fully automate their operations and benefit from the next global economic revolution.
“We believe in a future where the new normal of Globalisation will leave no one behind. When innovation meets inclusion, everyone can pursue their opportunities like the big guys did in the past,” Yang said.
The ninth WIF, the UN’s flagship forum for the global investment community, brings together policymakers, investors and business leaders to explore how investment can support sustainable, resilient and inclusive growth amid geopolitical fragmentation and rapid technological change.

title: Designing Payment Gateway Failover for the Day Your Acquirer Goes Down
summary:
On 20 October 2026, Revolut, Halifax and Lloyds banking apps went down together with Vinted and Rightmove, reportedly after an issue at a Google data center in London. Different companies, different products, one shared point of failure underneath. For any business that takes payments, this is the scenario this article is about.
A second acquirer is a sensible safeguard for the day the first one goes down. On its own, though, it helps only if something switches payments to it automatically, within seconds, before customers abandon checkout.
That switching mechanism is payment gateway failover. The second acquirer is redundancy; failover is what makes it useful at 7 p.m. on a Monday, when the first one starts timing out. This column covers how to design it: how to detect a failing acquirer, where to reroute payments, and how to avoid double charges.
Separate payment gateway failover from spare capacity
Let me draw the line: Acquirer redundancy is something you own: a contract, credentials, a certified integration. Failover is something that happens: a decision path that moves live traffic onto that capacity without waiting for a person.
A common and understandable setup is the first, with a manual version of the second: an engineer knows which configuration flag to change. That works well when they are available, and the problem is clear. The limit is time. A manual switch needs someone reachable and certain, and that costs minutes a checkout page does not have.
The gap shows up across six layers, and I would check each one separately.

Map the four ways an acquirer fails
When someone tells me 'the acquirer is down', I ask which of four things they mean, because each calls for a different response.
Hard outage. Connections refused, 5xx errors, or timeouts on every request. This is the easy one, and the only mode a basic uptime check reliably catches.
Brownout. Latency climbs, a share of requests time out and approval rate sags, while the endpoint still answers. 
Scoped failure. One MID, one currency, one payment method, one card brand or one issuer corridor breaks while everything else works. Velocity limits, risk holds, an expired connector certificate, and local scheme gateway problems all behave this way. A provider-level health check says healthy; a route-level one does not.
Upstream dependency failure. The acquirer is fine, and something beneath it is not: a cloud region, a 3D Secure (3DS) directory server, the scheme network, or the sponsor bank. 
Detect brownouts before they become outages
Health is best measured where failures actually happen: the route. A route is the combination of acquirer, MID, payment method, currency and, where it matters, card brand or issuer region. A circuit per provider is too coarse for scoped failures, and a circuit per merchant is too noisy to trust.
Five signals, combined, give a reliable picture:
Technical errors: connection failures, 5xx responses, and timeouts as a share of attempts in a sliding window.
Latency: p95 and p99 against the route's own baseline, not a global figure.
Infrastructure response codes: ISO 8583 codes such as 91 (issuer or switch inoperative) and 96 (system malfunction), which point at plumbing rather than the cardholder.
Approval rate against expectation: deviation from a rolling same-hour baseline per route, with a minimum sample size so a quiet route at 3 a.m. does not trip.
Synthetic probes: low-value authorizations or sandbox calls on idle routes, so you know the health of the secondary before you need it.
One rule should never bend: issuer declines such as insufficient funds or 'do not honor' must not count against route health. If they do, a burst of ordinary declines opens the circuit and sends traffic to a second acquirer that will decline it just the same.
The detector also needs guardrails so it doesn't become the incident. Trip on a sustained breach across two windows, not a single spike. Use hysteresis, so the bar to close a circuit is higher than the bar to open it. After a cool-off, go half-open and send a small trickle of traffic to test the route. A circuit that flaps every ninety seconds does more damage than a steadily degraded route.
Route across MIDs and acquirers
A failover route has to be eligible, funded, and portable before it is ever used. Four design decisions settle that. They also separate, in my view, an orchestrator that supports PSP failover across multiple MIDs from one that merely lists several connectors.
Fail over in tiers, starting at the MID
The MID is the smallest unit of failure that matters. When one MID hits a velocity limit, a risk hold or a descriptor problem, the cheapest recovery is a sibling MID at the same acquirer: same integration, same issuer relationships, no cross-provider state to move. When the acquirer itself degrades, the next tier is a second acquirer in the same region. When the region fails, the third tier is an acquirer with local presence elsewhere. Express these tiers per route. A single global fallback treats a MID limit and an acquirer outage as the same event, and it sends traffic to the wrong place in at least one of them.
Keep the second route warm
A standby that has never carried traffic is an untested hypothesis. Send the second route a steady slice (5–10% is a reasonable starting point) so that credentials, limits, 3DS settings, and issuer behavior are proven in production. The price is split volume, so read the primary contract for tiers and minimums before sizing it. Size the secondary for the primary's peak, not its average, and get throughput and limit headroom confirmed in writing.
Make tokens and authentication data portable
Two dependencies quietly turn a multi-acquirer setup into a single-acquirer one, and people discover them during the incident. The first is card-on-file tokens. A token held in one PSP's vault cannot be sent to another acquirer, so subscriptions and one-click checkouts fail over only if you hold the credentials yourself, use a portable token service, or use network tokens provisioned under a requestor identity you control.
The second is 3DS. Authentication data (CAVV, ECI, and the directory server transaction ID) can travel to a second acquirer only when authentication ran on an independent 3DS server. With a 3DS service bundled into the first acquirer, the customer has to authenticate again, a conversion hit that lands exactly when the shopper is already having a bad evening.
Wire failover and cascading together
They share plumbing and fire on different events, so keep them conceptually apart. Failover is triggered by route health and moves a share of traffic. Cascading is triggered by one soft decline and retries that single payment on the next route. Cascading limits the damage while the detector is still deciding; failover stops the loss once it has decided.
The same machinery earns its keep on ordinary days, because a decline at one acquirer is often an approval at another. The condition is discipline: retry only what is recoverable, such as provider-side failures, technical errors, and over-strict risk filters. A hard decline ends the chain, and scheme reattempt rules still apply.
Protect customers from double charges
This part is easy to overlook, and it is where failover can do harm. Failing over a transaction that has not been sent is easy. The hard cases are the ones sent and left unanswered, where the orchestrator does not know whether the acquirer authorized the payment. What it knows decides what it may safely do.

The rule for an unanswered payment is simple: check its status before any second attempt. If the first acquirer approved it, reverse it or return that result. Two habits make this work. Every attempt carries the same payment ID (an idempotency key), so all attempts link to one payment. And reconciliation across both acquirers catches stray approvals, so they are released before they reach the customer's statement.
Return traffic to the original acquirer gradually once it recovers, for example 10%, 25%, 50%, then full volume. Switching everything back at once is a reliable way to cause a second incident.
Test failover before the outage does
Run a drill: switch one route off during a quiet hour and time how long the system takes to detect the problem, switch traffic, and recover. Then check that both acquirers do not share a cloud region or a 3D Secure provider. If they do, they fail together.
For EU financial institutions, DORA's Chapter V also requires a concentration-risk assessment before contracting ICT services and documented exit strategies for critical ones. Merchants sit mostly outside that scope, but their PSPs and banks do not, and those obligations flow into supplier contracts.
Require these capabilities from an orchestrator
Whether the layer is built or bought, ask for a live demonstration of each of these:
Health tracked for each route: acquirer, MID, method, and currency.
Failover and retries as separate rules.
Control over which declines are retried and which stop.
A status check for unanswered payments, with reversal where needed.
Tokens and 3D Secure data that work with any acquirer.
A log of every attempt tied to one payment, plus a way to test failover and failback.
Enough connectors that a second acquirer exists for your method, currency, and region.
At Corefy, we work at this layer, above the acquirers. With routing & cascading, you connect a backup provider for each key method and currency, set the retry order, and choose which decline resolutions trigger a retry, with up to five attempts by default. Attempt-level logs separate recoverable declines from genuine ones, and our 650+ provider integrations make a second acquirer easier to find. Whichever vendor you evaluate, ours included, ask to see a forced failover live.
Check these five things before the next outage
If you take one list away from this article, make it this one:
Health is measured per route and catches slow degradation, not just downtime.
Every key route has a warm second route in a different failure domain.
Tokens and 3D Secure data move with the payment.
An unanswered payment is always checked before it is retried.
A drill this quarter has timed detection, switching and recovery.
A second acquirer is the cheapest part of resilience. The five checks above are what make it usable. To see how they map onto your current stack, talk to a Corefy payment expert.

Implementing automated failover mechanisms, maintaining warm secondary routes, ensuring portable tokens and 3D Secure data, and checking unanswered payments for double charges are essential steps to maintain continuous checkout operations and prevent customer loss.

title: DTCC Tokenization Service Goes Live, Marking Major Milestone in the Adoption of Digital Assets
summary:
The Depository Trust Company (DTC), a subsidiary of The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), the premier post-trade market infrastructure for the global financial services industry, today launched the DTCC Tokenization Service (DTS). The service brings tokenized securities into regulated financial markets through trusted, resilient and scalable market infrastructure, enabling investors to move assets more efficiently, access new liquidity pools and mobilize collateral within minutes.
DTS enables the minting of tokenized representations of real-world assets held at DTC. By leveraging the service, eligible users can take advantage of DTC-tokenized securities entitlements that can be converted between traditional and tokenized forms and delivered to users’ digital wallets of choice. Tokenized securities, or digital twins, retain the ownership rights, investor protections and economic entitlements as their traditional counterparts. DTC has more than $114 trillion in assets under custody.
“Today marks the culmination of years of work to bring tokenized securities into a regulated framework supported by trusted market infrastructure,” said Frank La Salla, President and CEO of DTCC. “By extending DTC’s resiliency, governance and operational standards into digital markets, we are establishing the foundation for responsible institutional adoption at scale.”
To date, 20 DTC Participants (clients) have signed agreements to access DTS including Alpaca, Apex Clearing Corporation, Barclays, Bank of America, BNP Paribas, Brown Brothers Harriman, Citadel Securities, Citi, Clear Street, DriveWealth, Edward Jones, Fidelity Investments, Interchange Clearing, J.P. Morgan, Marex, Mirae Asset Securities (USA) Inc., Morgan Stanley, State Street, UBS and Velocity Capital LLC. Future users will be onboarded on a rolling basis.
Created by the Markets, For the Markets
Consistent with DTC’s role as a critical market infrastructure provider, DTS was created in close collaboration with the industry it is designed to serve. Developed with input from more than 150 firms in the DTC Digital Assets Solutions Industry Working Group, DTS combines institutional-grade controls, established governance and operational safeguards to support adoption and convertibility across traditional and digital markets.
“The breadth of engagement across traditional finance and digital asset markets demonstrates that the industry is ready to move beyond experimentation and toward practical adoption,” said Brian Steele, Managing Director, President of Clearing & Securities Services at DTCC. “Working with more than 150 firms in our Industry Working Group, we built a service designed to support institutional use of tokenized securities at scale within a trusted operational framework.”                 
Supporting a New Interoperable Financial Ecosystem
DTS employs a multi-network, interoperable model designed to give firms greater scope to transact across traditional and digital environments. This model allows market participants to convert and deploy their assets seamlessly across traditional and tokenized markets, promoting ongoing liquidity in traditional markets while expanding it via the tokenized service. The service is currently integrated with the Canton Network and DTCC’s private Besu network, with additional blockchain networks to be added in 2027.
Beyond the DTC Participants that will use DTS directly, DTCC convened a broad digital asset ecosystem encompassing market participants, wallet providers, applications and technology firms to support greater interoperability and connectivity as digital markets and tokenization use cases evolve. Collaborators and partners include BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A., Blockdaemon, Broadridge, DFNS, DRW, Fireblocks, HIFI, Kaleido, Matter Labs, Ondo, Prometheum Capital, Talos, Taurus, Tradeweb, Transcend and Virtu.
“Today’s launch demonstrates what can be achieved through sustained industry collaboration, regulatory engagement and a disciplined approach to innovation,” said Nadine Chakar, Managing Director, Global Head of DTCC Digital Assets. “This is only the beginning of DTCC’s ultimate goal to build the Web3 ecosystem of the future that bridges established, trusted market infrastructure and digital ledger technology.”
The delivery of the DTCC Tokenization Service is the culmination of regulatory engagement, extensive industry collaboration and real-world validation to create a practical path for the adoption of tokenized securities. In December 2025, DTC received a No-Action Letter from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission authorizing it to tokenize Russell 1000 constituents, exchange-traded funds tracking major indices, and U.S. Treasury securities. About seven months later, DTCC and more than 30 firms completed initial limited-production trades and multiple on-chain transactions.

title: Hummingbird Acquires Quantimon to Bring Machine Learning to AML Transaction Monitoring for the Agentic Era
summary:
Hummingbird, the AI-powered orchestration platform for financial crime compliance, today announced the acquisition of Quantimon, the machine learning platform for AML risk detection. The acquisition deepens Hummingbird's investment in transaction monitoring, bringing machine learning models that learn from alert outcomes and federated learning technology onto the same platform where compliance teams resolve those alerts.
Most anti-money laundering (AML) transaction monitoring still runs on rules, and most of the alerts those rules generate turn out to be nothing. Machine learning has been slow to help because models need labeled outcomes and, at most institutions, those outcomes sit in case notes that are too expensive to turn into training data. That’s changing with AI. When AI agents and compliance analysts work alerts in Hummingbird, each disposition is recorded in a structured form a model can learn from. With Quantimon integrated into the platform, those dispositions feed back into detection and improve it. 
"AI has changed how compliance teams investigate financial crime, but the systems generating the alerts have stayed largely the same," said Joe Robinson, co-founder and CEO of Hummingbird. "Today our customers can clear alerts faster than ever, but they shouldn’t have to spend that capacity on noise. With Quantimon, every alert worked by an AI agent or analyst sharpens detection, so more of the alerts that reach our customers will be ones worth their time.” 
Quantimon’s machine learning models learn from how alerts are resolved, leveraging an institution’s own data in a closed feedback loop. The company also built a federated learning network, designed to let compliance teams benefit from patterns seen across other institutions without sharing customer data. 
"At Apple, Xoom, and PayPal, we watched our compliance teams spend their days working on seemingly endless alert backlogs. We started Quantimon to fix that at the source," said Ben Duranske, co-founder and CEO of Quantimon. "I’m thrilled Quantimon is joining Hummingbird, where our technology can be at the center of a loop that makes both detection and investigation smarter."
The Quantimon team is joining Hummingbird to enhance the platform’s transaction monitoring solution. Customers can expect:
Richer rule-based detection: Rules that are easier to build, test, and manage for larger and more complex monitoring programs. Strong rule coverage in AML is the foundation on which machine learning works best.
Machine learning models trained on each institution's alert outcomes: Models that learn from what a team decides to close, escalate, or file on, so alerts can be ranked by risk and activity that resembles confirmed cases can be caught even when no rule fires.
A network that sees beyond an institution's own walls: Over time, customers will be able to draw on signals from third-party intelligence or patterns across the wider Hummingbird network, so teams can detect risks they didn’t even know to look for.

title: Lloyds Uses Agentic AI Platform to Strengthen Customer Fraud Support
summary:
Lloyds expands agentic AI platform to strengthen customer fraud support after it supported fraud specialists across more than 10,600 live customer cases in 90 days. 
The platform, which helps colleagues investigate suspected debit card fraud, has improved its overall decision accuracy to over 90% in September, helping customers reach a resolution quicker. 
Improved through use in more than 10,600 customer cases
Lloyds improved the platform by testing its outputs against completed case outcomes and using feedback from fraud specialists to refine how it identifies relevant information, assesses fraud indicators and presents suggested actions. Over 90 days, 50 improvements were delivered through seven updates, contributing to more consistent recommendations and fewer false alarms and missed fraud cases.
The platform has achieved over 90% overall decision accuracy. In cases where it identified suspected fraud, more than 90% were subsequently confirmed as fraud. In simple terms, it is getting better at confirming more accurately when a transaction flagged as fraud really is fraud following interaction with our customers thereby reducing avoidable losses and improving the customer experience. 
As performance improves, Lloyds is continuing to test and monitor the platform before expanding its use in line with Lloyds’ Responsible AI approach, the technology supports rather than replaces colleague judgement. Trained fraud specialists review the evidence and suggested actions and remain accountable for the customer decision.
A simpler experience when customers need support
When a customer contacts Lloyds about suspected fraud, specialists can need information from multiple systems to understand what has happened and decide what action to take. The agentic AI platform brings more of that information together, assess relevant fraud indicators and recommends next steps, allowing the specialist to focus on the customer while remaining responsible for the final decision.
Fewer systems, faster support
The platform has already roughly halved the number of systems fraud specialists need to use during a customer call, from a process that previously required information across 12 to 15 systems. Lloyds aims to reduce this further to two or three systems by the end of the year. Over time, the bank aims to bring the information and actions needed for each case into one AI-enabled workspace.
How the AI works
The platform uses a group of specialist AI agents, each designed to support a different part of a fraud investigation. A central system coordinates their work and guides fraud specialists through up to nine stages of a case. By bringing relevant information and actions together, the technology helps colleagues investigate suspected fraud through a more joined-up process.
The reduction in overrides means that colleagues are increasingly able to use the platform’s recommended decisions without changing them, meaning customers get the right fraud decisions quicker.
Supporting Lloyds’ wider use of AI
The fraud AI platform is one example of how Lloyds is introducing next-generation AI across the business. Components developed for the platform are already being reused across other fraud journeys, helping teams move faster as the capability expands and could support further reuse in future, including in areas such as quality assurance. Taken together, these AI programmes are expected to contribute more than £100 million in additional value during 2026.

Fraud investigations involve multiple checks and decisions. This technology uses specialist AI agents to handle different parts of that process, while a central system coordinates their work and gives our fraud specialists the information they need in one place.
The improvement in accuracy shows the value of testing the technology in real customer cases, listening to the people using it and updating it regularly. We will continue to track how accurately it identifies fraud as we develop the platform further.
Rohit DhawanGroup Head of AI and Advanced Analytics at Lloyds

content_ta: முன்னாள் Aptos ஆலோசகர் Buzz, அந்த கிரிப்டோ திட்டத்திலிருந்து அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாக விலகியுள்ளார். அவர் தனது மீம் அடிப்படையிலான பிரச்சாரத்தையும் கவனத்தையும் இப்போது Facebook-ன் தாய் நிறுவனமான Meta மீது திருப்பியுள்ளார். இந்த எதிர்பாராத மாற்றம், பிளாக்செயின் சுற்றுச்சூழல் அமைப்பிலிருந்து பாரம்பரிய பெருநிறுவன தொழில்நுட்பப் பங்குகளுக்கு மாறியுள்ளதை குறிக்கிறது.

title: Wall Street’s Fast Money Fled Bitcoin ETFs, Sovereign Funds Stepped In
summary:
Hedge funds' BTC ETF sell-off highlights a strategic shift towards yield optimization, impacting market sentiment and institutional dynamics.
The post Galaxy Research says nine hedge funds and banks cut 68,000 BTC of spot ETF exposure appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: A recent report by Galaxy Research reveals that several hedge funds and major banks significantly reduced their Bitcoin spot ETF exposure by selling off tens of thousands of BTC. While fast money exited these products, sovereign wealth funds stepped in, highlighting an ongoing institutional shift toward long-term yield optimization and changing market dynamics within the cryptocurrency sector.
content_ta: Galaxy Research வெளியிட்ட புதிய அறிக்கையின்படி, பல ஹெட் ஃபண்டுகளும் பெரிய வங்கிகளும் தங்கள் வசம் இருந்த Bitcoin ஸ்பாட் ETF பங்குகளை பெருமளவில் விற்றுத் தள்ளியுள்ளன. குறுகிய கால முதலீட்டாளர்கள் வெளியேறிய போதிலும், இறையாண்மை நிதிகள் (Sovereign Funds) இதில் முதலீடு செய்ய முன்வந்துள்ளன. இது கிரிப்டோகரன்சி சந்தையில் நீண்ட கால முதலீட்டு உத்திகளில் ஏற்பட்டுள்ள மாற்றத்தைக் காட்டுகிறது.

title: Coinbase adds Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin across retail, exchange and Prime platforms
summary: RLUSD is live on Coinbase with 1:1 USD conversion on XRP Ledger, Ethereum and Base, capping a big week of news for Ripple.
content: Coinbase has integrated Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin across its retail, exchange, and Prime platforms. The stablecoin offers a one-to-one US dollar conversion and operates on multiple networks including the XRP Ledger, Ethereum, and Base. This launch marks a major milestone following a busy week of significant news for Ripple.
content_ta: Coinbase தனது retail, exchange மற்றும் Prime தளங்களில் Ripple-ன் RLUSD stablecoin-ஐ இணைத்துள்ளது. இந்த stablecoin ஒன்றுக்கு ஒன்று என்ற விகிதத்தில் US dollar மாற்றீட்டை வழங்குகிறது மற்றும் XRP Ledger, Ethereum மற்றும் Base உள்ளிட்ட பல நெட்வொர்க்குகளில் செயல்படுகிறது. இந்த வெளியீடு Ripple-க்கு ஒரு முக்கியமான வாரத்தைத் தொடர்ந்து வந்துள்ளது.

title: Galaxy’s AI data centers bring $79 million in lease revenue and a small net loss

content_ta: Galaxy-ன் AI டேட்டா சென்டர்கள் முதல் முழு Helios லீஸ் காலாண்டில் 79 மில்லியன் டாலர் லீஸ் வருவாயை ஈட்டியுள்ளன. இருப்பினும், இந்தப் பிரிவு 435,000 டாலர் சிறிய நிகர இழப்பைச் சந்தித்துள்ளது. இதற்கிடையில், Treasury மற்றும் Corporate துறைகள் நிறுவனத்தின் ஒட்டுமொத்த மீட்சிக்கு உதவின.

While the European Central Bank describes this decline as moderate, analysts note that any potential impact on Bitcoin and the broader digital asset market will depend heavily on prevailing financing costs and shifting investor risk appetites.
content_ta: யூரோ பகுதி வங்கிகள் சில்லறை நிதி அணுகலில் சாதனை அளவிலான சரிவை சந்தித்துள்ளதாக சமீபத்திய தரவுகள் தெரிவிக்கின்றன. இந்த சரிவை ஐரோப்பிய மத்திய வங்கி மிதமானது என்று விவரித்தாலும், Bitcoin மற்றும் பரந்த டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து சந்தையில் இதன் தாக்கம் நிதியளிப்பு செலவுகள் மற்றும் முதலீட்டாளர்களின் ஆபத்து எடுக்கும் திறனைப் பொறுத்து அமையும் என்று பகுப்பாய்வாளர்கள் குறிப்பிடுகின்றனர்.

title: Ethereum client security fixes leave binary users with a separate Java check
summary:
Teku and Besu Docker releases fix certificate trust, while binary users need to check their separately installed Java runtime.
Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: Recent security fixes for Ethereum clients Teku and Besu address certificate trust issues in Docker releases. However, users running binary versions must manually check their separately installed Java runtime to ensure full protection. This update is important for node operators maintaining network security and stability across these prominent Ethereum clients.
content_ta: Ethereum கிளைன்ட்களான Teku மற்றும் Besu இன் Docker வெளியீடுகளில் சான்றிதழ் நம்பகத்தன்மை சிக்கல்களைச் சரிசெய்ய புதிய பாதுகாப்புத் திருத்தங்கள் வெளியிடப்பட்டுள்ளன. இருப்பினும், பைனரி பதிப்புகளைப் பயன்படுத்துபவர்கள் தங்களது தனிப்பட்ட Java ரன்டைமைச் சரிபார்க்க வேண்டும். இந்த அப்டேட் பிணையப் பாதுகாப்பைப் பேண மிகவும் அவசியமானது.

title: OCC Proposes Weekly and Quarterly Reporting Forms for Stablecoin Issuers
summary: The OCC has published revised reporting forms intended to let supervisors monitor the financial condition and activity of permitted payment-stablecoin issuers.
tags: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
content: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has proposed new weekly and quarterly reporting forms for stablecoin issuers. These revised forms are designed to help supervisors effectively monitor the financial condition and operational activity of permitted payment-stablecoin issuers.
content_ta: Stablecoin issuers-களுக்கான புதிய வாராந்திர மற்றும் காலாண்டு அறிக்கை படிவங்களை Office of the Comptroller of the Currency முன்மொழிந்துள்ளது. அனுமதிக்கப்பட்ட payment-stablecoin issuers-களின் நிதி நிலை மற்றும் செயல்பாட்டு நடவடிக்கைகளை மேற்பார்வையாளர்கள் திறம்பட கண்காணிக்க இந்த திருத்தப்பட்ட படிவங்கள் உதவும்.

title: Bitcoin (BTC) Shows a ‘Major Sign of Strength:’ Price Rally Incoming?
summary: One whale has placed a huge BTC bet ahead of the FOMC meeting, but does that guarantee a price increase?
content: A prominent crypto whale has placed a massive Bitcoin bet ahead of the upcoming FOMC meeting, sparking market optimism. Analysts point to this large transaction as a major sign of strength for the digital asset. However, questions remain among investors about whether this heavy positioning guarantees a sustained price rally in the near future.
content_ta: வரவிருக்கும் FOMC கூட்டத்திற்கு முன்னதாக ஒரு முக்கிய crypto whale மிகப்பெரிய அளவில் Bitcoin முதலீட்டை மேற்கொண்டுள்ளது, இது சந்தையில் நம்பிக்கையை ஏற்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இந்த பெரிய பரிவர்த்தனையை ஆய்வாளர்கள் டிஜிட்டல் சொத்தின் வலிமையின் முக்கிய அறிகுறியாக சுட்டிக்காட்டுகின்றனர். இருப்பினும், இந்த முதலீடு அருகில் உள்ள காலத்தில் விலை உயர்வுக்கு உத்தரவாதம் அளிக்குமா என்பது குறித்து முதலீட்டாளர்கள் மத்தியில் கேள்விகள் தொடர்கின்றன.

title: CASHCAT surges 15%, but sellers lurk: What are the next key levels?
summary: CashCat indicators show weak buying pressure as perpetual market capital shrinks.
content: CASHCAT recently experienced a 15% price surge, drawing significant market attention. However, selling pressure remains a concern for traders. Technical indicators suggest that buying momentum is relatively weak, which is further reflected by a shrinking perpetual market capitalization. Market participants are closely monitoring key price levels to determine the next directional move for the token.
content_ta: CASHCAT விலையில் சமீபத்தில் 15% உயர்வு ஏற்பட்டுள்ளது, இது சந்தையின் கவனத்தை ஈர்த்துள்ளது. இருப்பினும், விற்பனை அழுத்தம் வர்த்தகர்களுக்கு ஒரு கவலைக்குரிய விஷயமாக உள்ளது. வாங்கும் வேகம் குறைவாகவே உள்ளதாக தொழில்நுட்ப குறிகாட்டிகள் குறிக்கின்றன, இது பெர்பச்சுவல் சந்தை மூலதனம் சுருங்குவதாலும் வெளிப்படுகிறது. டோக்கனின் அடுத்த கட்ட நகர்வை தீர்மானிக்க வர்த்தகர்கள் முக்கிய விலை நிலைகளை உன்னிப்பாக கவனித்து வருகின்றனர்.

title: Itaú formalizes crypto trading business under Brazil’s new rules
summary: Brazil’s new framework is reshaping oversight of crypto services, including the trading business Itaú launched in 2023.
content: Itaú has formalized its crypto trading business following the implementation of Brazil's new regulatory framework. The updated rules are reshaping the oversight of cryptocurrency services in the country, integrating the digital asset trading operations that the institution originally launched in 2023 under clearer compliance guidelines.
content_ta: Brazil-ன் புதிய ஒழுங்குமுறை விதிகளின் கீழ் Ita நிறுவனம் தனது crypto வர்த்தக வணிகத்தை அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாக்கியுள்ளது. இந்த புதிய கட்டமைப்பு நாட்டில் உள்ள cryptocurrency சேவைகளுக்கான மேற்பார்வையை மாற்றியமைக்கிறது, மேலும் 2023-ல் தொடங்கப்பட்ட இந்த நிறுவனத்தின் டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து வர்த்தக நடவடிக்கைகளை தெளிவான இணக்க வழிகாட்டுதல்களின் கீழ் கொண்டுவருகிறது.

title: BlackRock Resumes Buying Bitcoin as Price Reclaims $81,000
summary: BlackRock spends over $151 million on new Bitcoin purchase as its Bitcoin ETF records a fresh influx of new capital amid growing demand.
content: BlackRock has resumed purchasing Bitcoin as the price of the cryptocurrency reclaimed the $81,000 level. The major asset manager spent over $151 million on the new acquisition. This purchase coincides with its Bitcoin ETF recording a fresh influx of new capital, driven by growing institutional demand.
content_ta: Bitcoin-ன் விலை $81,000-ஐ எட்டியுள்ள நிலையில், BlackRock நிறுவனம் மீண்டும் Bitcoin வாங்குவதைத் தொடங்கியுள்ளது. இந்த புதிய முதலீனுக்காக அந்த நிறுவனம் $151 மில்லியனுக்கும் அதிகமாக செலவிட்டுள்ளது. அதிகரித்து வரும் தேவையால், அதன் Bitcoin ETF-ல் புதிய முதலீடுகள் குவிகின்றன.

title: Forget AI: Wintermute Explains Why Bitcoin's Next Move Now Depends on Oil

content: Cryptocurrency market maker Wintermute suggests that Bitcoin's next major price movement may be driven more by crude oil markets than artificial intelligence. As oil prices experience potential spikes, analysts point to these energy market dynamics as a critical factor influencing Bitcoin's path, highlighting specific key levels for traders to monitor closely in the current macroeconomic climate.

content: TRX options have officially launched on Blockchain.com, providing global retail and institutional users with expanded access to the TRON ecosystem.
